title: Lagos Never Sleeps
teaser: Third Mainland traffic, a rooftop on Victoria Island, and a Swiss banker with a very dangerous offer.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Lagos. Third Mainland Bridge at six in the evening. Nothing on it moves except the danfo drivers' mouths.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the back of his car, Kolade Balogun reads the letter for the third time.

lines.speaker: letter
lines.text: Kolade. You wanted everything. Earn it. — G.O.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Earn it. Old man, I've been earning it since I was sixteen.

scenes.prompt: The traffic hasn't moved in twenty minutes.

choices.text: Call the widow. Lock in the board votes before anyone else lands.

response.speaker: ibiere
response.text: Kolade. You always were the practical one. Come and see me.

choices.text: Look up the other names under the seal.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Dalyop. Ebiowei. Lawan. And me. A gem trader, a boat captain, a Kano accountant and a banker. What were you building, Chief?

choices.text: "Driver. Victoria Island. I need a drink first."

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Grief can wait until the second bottle.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Victoria Island. A rooftop bar, the whole city lit up like money.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A video call from a private number: a woman with pale hair and Lake Geneva behind her.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: Monsieur Balogun. Elise Moreau, Banque Moreau. I managed Chief Okoro's private accounts for many years.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: His will is... complicated. Help me keep his accounts quiet for a few weeks, and I can make sure the crown goes to you.

lines.speaker: elise
lines.text: Lagos deserves a king. Don't you think?

scenes.prompt: The most dangerous offer of his life.

response.speaker: elise
response.text: I knew you were the clever one.

choices.text: "He was my godfather. Find another fool."

response.speaker: elise
response.text: A pity. Fools live longer, Monsieur.

choices.text: Pretend to accept. Record every word.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: Of course, Madame. Let's talk numbers.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: In his pocket, his phone is recording.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the drive to Lekki, a motorbike pulls level with his window. The rider lifts two fingers like a gun, taps the glass twice, and is gone into the traffic.

lines.speaker: phone
lines.text: A photo, from a private number: Kolade asleep in his own bed, taken last night. 'We keep our partners close, Monsieur.'

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He checks the cloud for his recording of Elise. Someone has already deleted it. Only the copy on his phone survived.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dawn on the beach at Lekki. The Atlantic doesn't care about crowns.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Two ways to play this. Fly straight to Port Harcourt and be first in the room.

lines.speaker: kolade
lines.text: Or fly north to Jos and meet the woman whose name the old man wrote twice.

choices.text: Fly to Jos. Meet Nabyen Dalyop.

response.speaker: narrator
response.text: Later he'll tell everyone it was strategy. It wasn't.

choices.text: Fly straight to Port Harcourt. Be first in the room.

response.speaker: kolade
response.text: In Lagos, the early bird doesn't just catch the worm. He buys the farm.

outcomes.title: A Deal in the Dark
outcomes.text: Kolade said yes to Elise Moreau. Lagos might get its king. But kings who are made by other people can be unmade by them too.

outcomes.title: Two Faces
outcomes.text: Kolade smiled at the wolf and kept the tape running. A dangerous game, played well. So far.

outcomes.title: Not for Sale
outcomes.text: Kolade turned Elise down. For once, the man who wanted everything wouldn't sell anything.

reflections.text: A Lagos banker is flying north for a woman he has never met.
The widow is in Kolade's pocket. Or he's in hers.

s_bride.title: A promised bride
s_bride.text: BRIDE. Thirty years ago, two fathers promised a Lagos boy a bride from the Plateau. The Chief tore the agreement up the day Nabyen was born.

m_lagos.title: Third Mainland at Dusk
m_lagos.text: Yellow danfos, a gold lagoon, and two words: earn it.

m_beach.title: Dawn at Lekki
m_beach.text: The Atlantic, a choice, and a woman he hadn't met yet.

k_voice_elise.title: Recording: Elise Moreau
k_voice_elise.text: 'Lagos deserves a king, Monsieur. And kings are made in Geneva.'
